rationale: ADR-conformance lens. Reads only, all at 7a490064. No mutation probes were needed, so no detached worktree was created. The spec's problem diagnosis is sound, and the ADR-0045 Context claims check out against the tree: the N-1 vs leg 9.5 contradiction, lowest-numbered vs lowest-depth selection, the follow-up-bead wording, the drifted installed skill, and byte-exact historical_skills. The ADR pricing is not sound. (1) The R4.3 ADR-0041 amendment misquotes its target. Item (c) never says 'first registered'. Items (a)-(e) are the REATTEST admissibility list, and reattest consumes reviewedHeadSHAForBead too (ReattestStatePanelContradiction). Yet R4.3 specifies FindLandedMerge only. That leaves a section 2(i) deadlock: FindLandedMerge returns NoEvidence, its recovery is 'mindspec reattest', and reattest still refuses on the stale panel SHA. (2) R4.2 contradicts ADR-0041's Spec-125 text ('a two-parent first-parent merge ... proves LANDED') and section 2(ii)'s 'first-parent chain SINCE the candidate merge'. Neither change is priced as an amendment. FindLandedMerge also feeds complete's merged-unclosed reconcile (which CLOSES beads), plan approve's provenance check, impl adopt and stale-open, and none of those blast-radius consumers is named. (3) R6 changes ADR-0041's fourth-verb clause in three ways: a scoped subset, required evidence, and a re-claim that proceeds with NO flag on an existing, agent-writable marker. That last one is a new fail-open bypass, yet R6 is marked 'APPLIED', not amended. (4) The ADR-0025 touchpoint is false. bd metadata is exported to the committed .beads/issues.jsonl (verified: existing mindspec_readiness_override markers are in the tracked JSONL), so R6.2's 4 KiB evidence text WILL be committed and pushed to main. (5) ADR-0035: R6.1's 'exact invocation' recovery line omits the required --evidence flag, so pasting it refuses again. R1.2's 'bd update --parent' recovery replaces an existing parent the agent did not name. R1.3/AC-3 do not pin a recovery line. R1.4 leaves a hedged recovery command, though `bd blocked --parent` exists. (6) ADR-0045 conflicts with ADR-0044 and does not say so. ADR-0044 makes conduct 'L4 skill-layer doctrine' and its Consequences say skills carry conduct fragments, but ADR-0045 section 4 bans rules and rationale from skills. ADR-0045 also amends more of ADR-0040 than the L4 definition (the 'where does this rule live?' default answer and the staging ratchet), and no back-pointer is added to ADR-0040. Accepted status for a wholly unimplemented ADR goes against ADR-0032's tri-state amendment, which says spec-introduced ADRs stay Proposed until they ship, and the spec gives no rationale. (7) Under ADR-0030 the R4.1 membership is inconsistent: findEpicForBeadFn sees parents only, and internal/validate/readiness cannot import internal/next (next imports readiness), so it cannot call 'R1.1's predicate'. A metadata.spec_id-only member is then silently exempted from MF-3, which is fail-open. None of these is a hard block. Each is fixable in spec text before planning.
concrete_changes_required: R4.3 / ADR Touchpoints: correct the amendment's 'from' text (ADR-0041 Spec-125 item (c) reads 'a registered panel's reviewed_head_sha equal to an exact match's second parent' — it never says 'first'; the first-registration veto is spec-125 R5 code behaviour). State that items (a)-(e) are the reattest admissibility list and that the read-side legs live in §2(ii).

R4.3: specify ReattestLandedMerge's datum-(c) semantics under the SET lookup (reattest.go also calls reviewedHeadSHAForBead and refuses with ReattestStatePanelContradiction). Make a stale non-matching registration non-corroborating there too, or the recovery chain deadlocks under ADR-0041 §2(i): AC-11 leg 3 → NoEvidence → 'mindspec reattest' → panel-contradiction refusal. Add an AC leg: two registrations {stale A, B=second parent} plus no tip/binding → reattest writes the binding; {A} only → reattest proceeds on datum (a) and does not refuse on A.

Price R4.2 as an ADR-0041 amendment too. The Spec-125 amendment binds landed-ness to 'a two-parent first-parent merge whose second parent EQUALS the bead's landed tip', and §2(ii) defines revert-awareness over 'the first-parent chain SINCE the candidate merge'. Both texts must be amended (reachable-from-tip; net content at tip). Also update the first-parent rationale in the SubsumptionConflict arm comment and the FirstParentMerges/ExactSecondParentMerges doc contracts.

Enumerate every FindLandedMerge/MergedUnclosed consumer whose behaviour R4.2/R4.3 changes, and state the intended effect on each: complete's merged-unclosed reconcile (mergedUnclosedFn; this CLOSES beads, the ADR-0041 §2(ii) case), approve/plan.go planFindLandedMergeFn, approve/adopt_lattice.go adoptFindLandedMergeFn (called on corroboratedRef), lifecycle/stale_open.go, and reattest. Add at least one AC pinning that the complete reconcile does not newly close a bead whose only corroboration is an off-first-parent merge reachable via a main-into-spec merge, or say why that is correct.
Fix OQ-4's grounding: reattest's nominator is reattest.go's own firstParentMergesFn scan, not gitutil.ExactSecondParentMerges (which only the executor's binding writer uses).

ADR-0041 amendment placement and landing: append a new 'Amendment (Spec 129)' section (precedent: §2(i)-(iii) Spec 121, §3(i) Spec 128, Amendment (Spec 125)) rather than rewriting the Spec-125 item (c) text in place. Cross-reference it from item (c), finalize it in the bead that lands the citing code (the Spec-125 precedent), and add an AC that pins the amendment text (as AC-17 does for ADR-0045).

R6 vs ADR-0041 fourth-verb clause: the clause says --allow-not-ready 'proceeds past a failing floor, emits a warning naming every failing signal'. R6.1 (subset rule, bare-flag refusal) and R6.2 (mandatory evidence) change that contract, so mark ADR-0041 AMENDED (fourth-verb clause), not APPLIED.

R6.3 re-claim leg: 'GateReadiness on a re-claim applies the subset rule to an existing marker, so an already-overridden bead does not demand a second override' opens a NEW flagless bypass. It is authorized by an agent-writable bd metadata key and records no new journal entry (ADR-0040 L1: a bypass goes 'through a journaled escape hatch'). Either require the explicit scoped flag on re-claim (evidence may be reused by sha), or price this as an ADR-0041 amendment, record a re-claim audit entry, and state the forged-marker threat. Today a forged marker has no gate effect; after R6.3 it opens the gate.

R6.3: define the handling of LEGACY markers (pre-129 {signals, overridden} with no evidence). The tracked JSONL already holds several MF-3 markers. Say how ready-check renders them and whether they satisfy the re-claim subset rule, given that R6.2 makes evidence mandatory.

ADR-0025 touchpoint is wrong: bd metadata is projected into the committed, pushed .beads/issues.jsonl (verified: mindspec_readiness_override markers are present in the tracked JSONL at 7a490064), so R6.2's evidence.text up to 4 KiB WILL be committed to every spec branch and to main. Either store only {path, sha256, bytes} plus a short escaped excerpt, or state the commitment explicitly, with a warning that the evidence file must not contain secrets, and fix the touchpoint sentence.

ADR-0035 R6.1: the refusal's 'recovery: <this exact invocation with --allow-not-ready=<ids>>' must also carry '--evidence <path>' (R6.2 makes it mandatory), or pasting the recovery refuses again (an ADR-0041 §2(i) deadlock). Pin it in AC-14.

ADR-0035 R1.2: 'bd update <id> --parent <epic-id>' REPLACES an existing parent the agent did not name when the near-miss already has a parent (the sentence itself prints 'parent: <parent-id>'). Emit it only when parent is none, and degrade to an inspection-first line (bd show <id> --json) otherwise, per the Spec-127 amendment item 2. Register the new emitted commands in internal/guard's registries as the recovery-convention lint requires.

ADR-0035 R1.3/AC-3: name the recovery line for both selector-on-empty refusals and assert in AC-3 that the final line matches '^recovery: '. R1.4: replace '(or the bd invocation the plan verifies exists)' with the verified 'bd blocked --parent <epic-id>' (it exists in bd 1.1.0).

ADR-0045 vs ADR-0044: ADR-0044 says conduct 'ships as skill/ADR text', is 'L4 skill-layer doctrine', and its Consequences have the five skills carry role-local conduct fragments. ADR-0045 §4 bans rules and rationale from skills. Add ADR-0044 to ADR-0045's Amends line, with the reconciliation stated (e.g. the conduct fragments move into the binary-owned 'panel brief' template under Decision 3), or state the carve-out.

ADR-0045 vs ADR-0040: the amendment covers more than 'the L4 definition'. It also replaces §1's 'start it at L4 if its correctness depends on judgment' default and the open-ended staging ratchet, now date-bound under Decision 5. Widen the Amends line accordingly, add a one-sentence reconciliation with ADR-0040 §3 ('never at the prompt-format level' vs binary-owned prompt templates), and add an 'Amended by ADR-0045' back-pointer blockquote in ADR-0040 §1 (precedent: ADR-0031/ADR-0036), listing ADR-0040.md in In Scope.

ADR-0045 status: justify 'Accepted' against ADR-0032's tri-state amendment (spec-introduced ADRs are 'legitimately Proposed until the implementation that validates them ships'; flipping early is the pressure it names). Either land it as Proposed and flip it at 129's impl approve, or record that Accepted means the operator-decided direction with zero shipped decisions, and that no 129 bead may cite ADR-0045 as coverage for anything beyond R1.4.
Impacted Domains: drop the option to mirror R1.4's rule into ms-spec-autopilot/skills. ADR-0045 §4, which lands in this same spec, forbids rules in skills.

R4.1 / ADR-0030 layering: findEpicForBeadFn (phase.FindEpicForBead) resolves only a parent-epic dependency, and internal/validate/readiness cannot import internal/next (next/ready_gate.go imports readiness), so 'a member per R1.1's predicate' is not callable from readiness. Put the single membership predicate in a package both can import (internal/bead or internal/phase, bd via internal/bead). Close the fail-open: a metadata.spec_id-only member (selectable under R1.1) must still be held to the landed-merge test, not PASS on bd-closed alone. Add an AC-9 leg for it.

R6.4: list the actual surfaces that state the bare/all-or-nothing form: ADR-0041 fourth-verb clause, .mindspec/core/USAGE.md (two places), .mindspec/core/WORKFLOW-STATE-MACHINE.md, .mindspec/domains/workflow/{architecture,interfaces,runbook}.md, and .mindspec/domains/execution/interfaces.md (the marker schema row gains evidence). autonomy.md does not mention the flag today.

findings.title: R4.3's ADR-0041 amendment misquotes and mis-targets item (c); reattest is unspecified, which leaves a deadlock
findings.detail: ADR-0041 Spec-125 item (c) text: 'a registered panel's reviewed_head_sha equal to an exact match's second parent', with no 'first'. Items (a)-(e) are reattest's admissibility list. reattest.go (around line 277) calls reviewedHeadSHAForBead and refuses with ReattestStatePanelContradiction on mismatch. R4.3 rewrites the helper as a SET but specifies only FindLandedMerge. With registrations {stale A} only, FindLandedMerge returns NoEvidence and the recovery is reattest. Under any reading where reattest keeps contradiction semantics, reattest refuses, which violates ADR-0041 §2(i).

findings.title: R4.2 broadens landed-ness beyond ADR-0041's first-parent text, unpriced, with unnamed CLOSE-path consumers
findings.detail: ADR-0041 Spec-125 amendment: 'git topology (a two-parent first-parent merge whose second parent EQUALS the bead's landed tip) proves it LANDED'. §2(ii): revert-awareness 'BY NET EFFECT: the first-parent chain SINCE the candidate merge'. R4.2 changes candidate discovery to every reachable merge. FindLandedMerge feeds complete.go's mergedUnclosedFn reconcile (closes beads), approve/plan.go planFindLandedMergeFn, approve/adopt_lattice.go adoptFindLandedMergeFn, and stale_open.go. The spec frames R4 as MF-3-only and names none of these. The in-code SubsumptionConflict rationale ('M is in the tip's first-parent history') also becomes stale.

findings.title: R6 changes ADR-0041's fourth-verb clause but is marked APPLIED; the re-claim leg is a new flagless, forgeable bypass
findings.detail: The fourth-verb clause: '--allow-not-ready override proceeds past a failing floor, emits a warning naming every failing signal, and records a durable override marker'. R6.1/R6.2 change that contract. R6.3 lets GateReadiness proceed on re-claim with NO flag when an existing marker covers the failing set. The marker is agent-writable bd metadata, and the gate never read it before 129, so a forged marker goes from having no gate effect to opening the gate. No new journal entry is recorded (ADR-0040 L1's 'journaled escape hatch').

findings.title: ADR-0025 touchpoint is false: the evidence text gets committed via the JSONL projection
findings.detail: The spec says R6's evidence file is 'stored in bd metadata, never committed as an artifact'. ADR-0025 §3: every executor commit refreshes .beads/issues.jsonl from Dolt. Verified: `git show 7a490064:.beads/issues.jsonl` contains mindspec_readiness_override objects. Up to 4 KiB of arbitrary operator file content therefore lands in git on the spec branch and on main via the PR.

findings.title: ADR-0035 recovery-line defects in R1.2, R1.3, R1.4 and R6.1
findings.detail: R6.1: the filled-in recovery omits the mandatory --evidence, so the paste refuses again. R1.2: 'bd update <id> --parent <epic>' replaces an existing parent the agent did not name (the near-miss sentence can print a non-none parent). The ADR-0035 Spec-127 amendment item 2 says to degrade to inspection-first. R1.3/AC-3: no recovery line is specified or asserted. R1.4: a hedged command, although `bd blocked --parent` is verified to exist in bd 1.1.0. New emitted commands need registry entries for the internal/guard convention lint.

findings.title: ADR-0045 conflicts with ADR-0044 and does not say so
findings.detail: ADR-0044 Related line: 'conduct is L4 skill-layer doctrine'. Its Context: 'Per ADR-0040, it ships as skill/ADR text'. Its Consequences: the five shipped skills carry role-local operational fragments plus a citation. ADR-0045 §4: a skill contains no rule ('must', 'never') and no rationale, and §3 moves review-with-a-lens prompts into binary templates. ADR-0045 lists ADR-0044 only as Related and states no amendment or reconciliation.

findings.title: ADR-0045's ADR-0040 amendment is understated and has no back-pointer
findings.detail: ADR-0045 claims to amend only ADR-0040 §1's L4 definition. It also overrides §1's 'where does this rule live? start it at L4 if its correctness depends on judgment' and makes the staging ratchet date-bound (Decision 5). It sits in tension with §3's 'never at the prompt-format level' and gives no reconciling sentence. ADR-0040 itself is not edited (repo precedent: 'Amended by' blockquotes in ADR-0031/0036) and is not in In Scope.

findings.title: ADR-0045 lands Accepted with zero shipped decisions, contrary to the ADR-0032 tri-state amendment's intent
findings.detail: ADR-0032 (PR #126 amendment): spec-introduced ADRs are 'legitimately Proposed until the implementation that validates them ships'. Flipping early is exactly the pressure it removed. ADR-0045's Verification section itself says that next-action, submit, prompt templates and the rule table do not exist. The Deciders field (Max) may justify Accepted, but the spec should record why and fence coverage citations.

findings.title: Skill-mirror option in Impacted Domains contradicts ADR-0045 §4
findings.detail: Impacted Domains allows mirroring R1.4's consumer rule into ms-spec-autopilot. ADR-0045, landing in the same spec, says a skill does not contain a rule.

findings.title: R4.1 membership is inconsistent with R1.1 and not reachable under the import graph, so a metadata-linked bead fails open on MF-3
findings.detail: phase.FindEpicForBead (findEpicForBeadFn) resolves only a parent-epic dependency. internal/next/ready_gate.go imports internal/validate/readiness, so readiness cannot import next.SpecMembers. A bead linked only by metadata.spec_id is a member (selectable, claimable, merged as bead/<id>) under R1.1, but a non-member under R4.1. Its closed dependents would then PASS MF-3 on bd-closed alone, which converts a fail-closed check into fail-open.

findings.title: Legacy override markers not addressed; R6.4 doc-surface list incomplete
findings.detail: The tracked JSONL already holds pre-129 {signals, overridden} markers with no evidence, and R6.3 does not define how they render or whether re-claim honours them. The bare-form statement appears in ADR-0041, USAGE.md, WORKFLOW-STATE-MACHINE.md, domains/workflow architecture/interfaces/runbook and domains/execution/interfaces.md. R6.4 names only bead_clarify.go and autonomy.md, and autonomy.md does not mention the flag at all.

findings.title: OQ-4 grounding slip
findings.detail: OQ-4 and R4.2 call ExactSecondParentMerges 'reattest's nominator'. In fact reattest.go runs its own firstParentMergesFn scan (around line 212), and ExactSecondParentMerges is used only by the executor's binding writer (mindspec_executor.go around lines 1669/1709). The routing decision OQ-4 defers therefore has the wrong function name.

findings.title: Verified OK
findings.detail: ADR-0045 Context claims hold at 7a490064: ms-bead-cycle '≥ N−1 APPROVE → merge terminal' (line 60), 'filed as a follow-up bead before merge'; ms-panel-tally 'floor, not a sufficient condition'; gate.go leg (9.5); bead-cycle lowest-numbered vs autopilot lowest-depth; the installed .claude ms-bead-cycle was last committed 2026-07-07 vs the plugin's 2026-07-24, and the files differ; previouslyShippedSkills uses byte-exact historical_skills. ADR-0030: the new git primitive in gitutil consumed by lifecycle, and bd via internal/bead, are conformant; `bd ready --metadata-field` and `--has-metadata-key` exist in bd 1.1.0.

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: (1) The BRIEF header tells reviewers to write '<your-slot>-round-1.json beside this BRIEF', which contradicts the dispatch prompt's scratch path and the BRIEF's own 'READ-ONLY on the repo' conduct rule. (2) Template residue: duplicate '## Summary' headings and unfilled TODO(skill) placeholders for Files in Scope, Acceptance Criteria (verbatim), Prior-Round Asks and Lens. The verbatim-AC section is the ADR-0044 provenance case (spec-121 summarized BRIEF). (3) The grounding file list omits internal/lifecycle/reattest.go, a direct consumer of reviewedHeadSHAForBead and the code home of ADR-0041 item (c) that R4.3 amends. It also omits the other FindLandedMerge consumers (internal/complete/complete.go mergedUnclosedFn, internal/approve/adopt_lattice.go). (4) The O2 lens frames R4.3 as the one ADR-0041 amendment; R4.2 and R6 also change ADR-0041 text.
